messages:
eli: Quick idea dump — we should try a "siren mode" at the edge for canary/A-B traffic. Lightweight, tenant-scoped, reversible, and auditable. Minimal central involvement unless escalation needed. Thoughts? :mag:

ravi: I like "siren" name :) Core: evaluate signals on a timer (not per-request), set an in-memory override for the tenant when score crosses threshold, use short probation TTL, and require consecutive healthy ticks to recover.

claire: +1. My list of constraints: 1) keep decision cheap (O(1) per tenant per tick). 2) prevent a single noisy tenant from flipping node-wide behavior. 3) provide clear traceable stamps for postmortems.

eli: Concrete primitives I want:
- probation_ttl_ms: 30000 (short lease)
- backoff_sequence_ms: [30000, 60000, 120000]
- recover_windows: 4 (need 4 healthy ticks)
- scope: tenant (default) or node (explicit opt-in)
- scoring: combine EWMA(error_rate) and EWMA(latency_ms) with configurable weights

ravi: Also add two escalation modes: soft_rollout (reduce max_tokens or route to quantized model) and hard_revert (switch to last-known-good). Soft is reversible quickly; hard is more durable and needs stronger signal/backoff.

claire: For safety, require a tenant-local bucket: token-bucket capacity=2 so a tenant can't flip more than 2 times per node in an hour. Also add node-level circuit breaker: max_hard_reverts_per_hour=3.

eli: Telemetry: when we apply an override emit a stamped event and set a trace header: x-edge-siren: inst=${INSTANCE_ID};reason=${REASON};policy=${POLICY_REV}. Also metric edge_siren_override_total{scope,reason,tenant,inst}.

ravi: Ownership split proposal: infra owns generic sampling and EWMA infra + default thresholds; runtime owns domain detectors and weight recommendations. Edge policy accepts both signal classes and exposes signal_weights. Default to 0.7 infra / 0.3 runtime for automatic hard_revert.

ops-bot: [lint] edge-siren-schema v1 validated. INFO: consider exposing "min_tick_interval_ms" for high churn clusters.

claire: One trick to reduce split-brain: add a randomized jitter in re-eval windows and require that a threshold breach be observed on >50% of sampled requests for that tenant on the node before immediate hard_revert. Soft_rollout can be triggered on single-window breaches.

eli: Example compact policy (YAML inline):
---
policy_version: "edge-siren-v1"
scope: "tenant"
signals:
  - infra_error_ewma(weight:0.6, alpha:0.18, window_ms:30000)
  - infra_p99_ewma_ms(weight:0.4, alpha:0.12, window_ms:60000)
  - runtime_hallucination_score(weight:0.3, sample_rate:0.01)
soft_rollout_threshold: 0.55
hard_revert_threshold: 0.87
probation_ttl_ms: 30000
backoff_sequence_ms: [30000,60000,120000]
recover_windows: 4
tenant_bucket_capacity: 2
node_max_hard_reverts_per_hour: 3
operator_force_key: "control-plane.force.edge_siren.v1"
---

ravi: For Dedicated/Private we keep same schema but allow control-plane to host policy; local agent pulls it. Add a compatibility flag to prevent operator_force_key if customer disables remote force.

claire: Action items: eli to write spec + proto for policy (this sprint). ravi to prototype evaluator tick and tenant token-bucket (PR). infra to publish EWMA helper lib and default thresholds. ops to add trace header + metrics dashboards. We'll run a small canary with soft_rollout only first.

eli: Open question: central reconcile behavior — my take: central watch only, can escalate to operator_force_key if majority of nodes report persistent hard_reverts. Keep central out of routine decision loop.

ops-bot: [note] scheduled canary test (edge-siren soft_rollout) in staging on 2026-03-01T09:00Z

claire: Nice. Let's keep numbers conservative for the trial and revise based on telemetry. Thanks all :thumbsup:
